nuances.title: 합쇼체 vs 해요체 register mismatch
nuances.ai_likely_does: Uses uniform 해요체 (-아요/-어요) throughout, or randomly mixes, treating it as the single 'polite' form
nuances.native_does: On a service call the customer leans 해요체 for requests (해 주세요, 될까요?) but naturally drops into clipped 합쇼체 at key moments (감사합니다, 부탁드립니다, 알겠습니다). Consistent, situation-appropriate level is the tell.

nuances.title: Over- or mis-applied subject honorific -시-
nuances.ai_likely_does: Sprinkles -시- everywhere or applies it to the customer's own actions (제가 예약하셨어요)
nuances.native_does: Customer never honorifics their own verbs (제가 예약했어요); applies -시- only to the agent/third party. Agent uses -시- on the customer's actions (고객님 예약하셨어요?).

nuances.title: Translationese for core service nouns
nuances.native_does: Uses established terms: 항공편 (flight), 예약 (booking), 환불 (refund), 취소 (cancellation), 변경 (change), 수수료 (fee). A calque instantly marks non-native.

nuances.title: Sino- vs native number system confusion
nuances.ai_likely_does: Picks one system; says 세 시간 as 삼 시간, or counts items with Sino (일, 이, 삼 개)
nuances.native_does: Hours use native (세 시간, 한 시), minutes use Sino (삼십 분); 두 명, 세 개 (native + counter) vs 삼 번, 오 층 (Sino). Mixing within one phrase (세 시 삼십 분) is the native default.

nuances.title: Wrong or omitted counters (분류사)
nuances.ai_likely_does: Drops counters or uses 개 for everything (사람 두 개, 표 한 개)
nuances.native_does: Selects the right counter: 두 분/두 명 (people, 분 honorific), 한 장 (tickets/cards), 한 건 (cases/bookings), 한 통 (calls). 예약 한 건, 항공권 두 장.

nuances.title: Verbalizing email @ . _ -
nuances.ai_likely_does: Reads '@' as '앳' literally, '.' as '닷', '_' as '언더스코어' in full English
nuances.native_does: @ = 골뱅이; . = 점; _ = 밑줄 (or 언더바); - = 붙임표 or 다시; e.g. gildong@naver.com → '길동 골뱅이 네이버 점 컴'. '골뱅이' for @ is the single biggest tell.

nuances.title: Phone number readout conventions
nuances.ai_likely_does: Reads 0 as '제로'/'영' inconsistently, says 공일공 vs reading clusters as large numbers
nuances.native_does: Reads digit-by-digit in Sino with 공 for 0 (공일공 = 010); 1588 read 일오팔팔. Korean uses 공, not 영 or 제로, on the phone.

nuances.title: Date format and reading (유월/시월)
nuances.ai_likely_does: Says dates in English order or uses native numbers for the day; reads month names wrong
nuances.native_does: Year-month-day, all Sino: 이천이십육년 유월 이십삼일. June=유월, October=시월 (irregular, not 육월/십월). Getting 유월/시월 right is a strong native marker.

nuances.title: Name order and title attachment
nuances.ai_likely_does: Western first-last order; attaches 씨 to family name only (김씨), or uses 씨 where service requires 고객님/님
nuances.native_does: Family name first (김길동); agent addresses customer as 고객님 or 길동 님, never 김 씨 alone (rude). Service register strongly prefers 고객님.

nuances.title: Konglish loanwords that ARE native vs over-correction
nuances.ai_likely_does: Either avoids all loanwords (says 표 awkwardly) or invents wrong ones
nuances.native_does: Uses naturalized loanwords where they're the norm: 마일리지, 체크인, 게이트, 포인트, 클레임 — but native words for 예약/환불/취소/좌석/창가. Knowing which slot takes the loanword is the skill.

nuances.title: Backchannel 네/예 frequency and form
nuances.ai_likely_does: Under-uses backchannels (English-style silent listening) or only says 네 once; never uses 예
nuances.native_does: Frequent 네…네 / 예 on every agent turn; 예 slightly more formal, 네 default. Strings like 네네 or 아 네 are natural. Absence reads as foreign.

nuances.title: Native hesitation fillers
nuances.ai_likely_does: Inserts English-shaped fillers or none; over-clean speech
nuances.native_does: Uses 그…, 저기요, 음…, 아 그, 뭐랄까, 잠시만요. 저기 / 저기요 as a softening opener to get attention is distinctly native.

nuances.title: Request softeners and grammar of asking
nuances.ai_likely_does: Direct calques: '도와줄 수 있어요?' / uses 원하다 for 'I want' (저는 환불을 원해요)
nuances.native_does: Native: 환불 받고 싶은데요 / 환불 좀 해 주세요 / 확인 좀 부탁드려요. The trailing -는데요 to soften and 좀 as a softener are essential; 원하다 sounds like a translated demand.

nuances.title: Call opening and closing formulae
nuances.ai_likely_does: Opens with bare '안녕하세요' then English-structured statement; closes with stiff '감사합니다 안녕히 계세요'
nuances.native_does: Opens 여보세요? then 안녕하세요, 문의 좀 드리려고 하는데요…; closes with 네 수고하세요 / 감사합니다. 여보세요 and 수고하세요 are native phone rituals.

nuances.title: Currency amounts in 만/억 grouping
nuances.ai_likely_does: Reads large won by Western thousands grouping (오십 천 원 for 50,000)
nuances.native_does: Groups by 만: 50,000 = 오만 원, 150,000 = 십오만 원, 1,200,000 = 백이십만 원. 오십 천 원 is impossible for a native. 원 always Sino.

nuances.title: Indirectness and -는데요 trailing
nuances.ai_likely_does: States needs as complete blunt sentences ('환불해 주세요. 이유는…') in English problem-then-request order
nuances.native_does: Trails off with -는데요 / -아서요 leaving the request implied (어제 결제가 두 번 됐는데요…). This collaborative incompleteness is core to Korean service talk.

nuances.title: Rising 네? vs flat 네
nuances.ai_likely_does: Produces flat intonation on 네 regardless, losing the question/agreement distinction
nuances.native_does: 네 (flat) = yes/agreement; 네? (sharp rise) = 'sorry, what?'; 네~ (long fall) = soft acknowledgment. A flat 네 where 네? is needed misfires the turn.

nuances.title: Sentence-final -요 rise vs fall (statement vs question)
nuances.ai_likely_does: Uses uniform intonation so 환불 됐어요 (statement) and 환불 됐어요? (question) sound identical
nuances.native_does: Korean often marks yes/no questions by rising intonation alone with identical -요 wording; the fall/rise on the final -요 distinguishes confirming vs asking (가능해요↘ vs 가능해요↗).
